source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Stroke can affect multiple functional domains, and coordinated interdisciplinary care addresses the full range of physical, cognitive, and communication needs","B":"An approach generally considered to rest on fairly little established supporting clinical evidence despite how widely it is actually used today","C":"Only the client's physical rehabilitation needs actually requiring dedicated attention from a trained healthcare professional during recovery","D":"Stroke recovery needs generally being limited to what a single clinical discipline alone can adequately and fully address on its own"}}
source_row.rationale: Interdisciplinary stroke care is important because stroke can affect multiple functional domains, and coordinated care from nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology addresses this full range of needs, supported by strong evidence for improved outcomes.
source_row.source_detail: Value of Coordinated Interdisciplinary Stroke Care
source_row.stem: A client recovering from stroke receives care from an interdisciplinary team, including nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology. This coordinated approach is important because:
